description.value: The study examined whether younger and older adults use similar neural mechanisms for cognitive reappraisal and whether age and individual differences in cognitive ability influence emotion-regulation-related brain activation and connectivity.

spans.text: Here we compared the neural mechanisms of cognitive reappraisal in younger and older adults.

design.value: Younger and older adults completed cognitive testing and a cognitive reappraisal task during fMRI. On trials with positive, negative, or neutral images, participants either experienced their emotions naturally or reappraised the image to decrease their emotional response; analyses examined condition effects, age-group differences, PPI connectivity, and cognition–activation relationships.

spans.text: Each person participated in two sessions on different days. The first session included a psychometric testing battery and training on our emotional reappraisal paradigm, and the second session involved fMRI scanning.
All images were drawn from the International Affective Picture System ( Lang et al. , 2005 ).
